name: Humain

summary.text: HUMAIN is a Saudi artificial-intelligence company announced by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman on May 12, 2025 as wholly owned by the Public Investment Fund, which he chairs; it is intended to operate across the AI value chain, from data centres and cloud infrastructure to Arabic-language models, with Tareq Amin as chief executive. In May 2025 Nvidia agreed to supply it with chips for up to 500 megawatts of data centres and AMD announced a collaboration of up to $10 billion; on November 19, 2025 the U.S. Commerce Department authorised exports of up to 35,000 Nvidia Blackwell chips to it. In October 2025 PIF and Aramco signed a non-binding term sheet for Aramco to take a significant minority stake with PIF retaining the majority, and in 2026 HUMAIN said it had invested $3 billion in xAI's Series E ahead of xAI's merger with SpaceX. The PIF, Nvidia and xAI files on this site hold those deals; this file holds the company's own record.

facts.claim: PIF's press release of May 12, 2025 states that the Crown Prince, as Prime Minister and chairman of PIF's board, announced HUMAIN as a PIF-owned company that will operate and invest across the AI value chain as a unified operating company, including data centres, cloud infrastructure and Arabic-language large language models.

PIF launches HUMAIN to lead Saudi AI infrastructure and Arabic LLM development

facts.claim: Tareq Amin is HUMAIN's chief executive; HUMAIN has said it aims at a dual listing on Nasdaq and the Saudi exchange within four years, and has announced deals with Nvidia, AMD, AWS, Qualcomm, Cisco, Groq and xAI and a planned $10 billion venture fund.

facts.claim: In late October 2025 PIF and Aramco signed a non-binding term sheet under which Aramco would acquire a significant minority stake in HUMAIN, both parties would contribute AI assets, capabilities and staff, and PIF would retain majority ownership; the deal is subject to definitive agreements and regulatory approvals.

facts.claim: On November 19, 2025 the U.S. Commerce Department announced it had authorised exports of advanced semiconductors to HUMAIN in Saudi Arabia and G42 in the UAE, each approved to buy the equivalent of up to 35,000 Nvidia Blackwell GB300 chips, subject to security and reporting conditions.
